Content: This question has `bbtext(two)` parts. First, answer Part A. Then, answer Part B.
What is the position of the author of Passage 1 regarding the use of biofuels?

A.Choice: Newer biofuels have the ability to generate more power than traditional fossil fuels.

B.Choice: Biofuels provide solutions to issues of waste management and limited energy.

C.Choice: Nearly any biological material or waste product can produce biofuels.

D.Choice: Biofuel production mimics a natural process with faster results.

Content: Which detail from Passage 1 supports the response in Part A?

A.Choice: “A company in Idaho makes ethanol using potato waste from a nearby potato processing plant. A cheese factory in California makes it from unused whey.” (paragraph 4)

B.Choice: “When used as a substitute for petroleum, it reduces total air pollution by more than 50 percent and cancer-causing substances in the exhaust by 94 percent.” (paragraph 5)

C.Choice: “Most intriguing of all is the oil produced by a machine developed by Changing World Technologies that uses a thermal depolymerization process (TDP) to take materials apart at the molecular level.” (paragraph 6)

D.Choice: “Although producing biofuels generally costs more than pumping petroleum out of the Earth, the added cost is offset by many benefits.” (paragraph 8)

Content: In Passage 2, the author argues that corn ethanol production takes the focus away from important food production. Select `bbtext(before)` the sentence below that supports this claim.

:ibox:	 :MC-A: The problem with corn ethanol is that it takes about the same amount of fossil fuel to produce an equal amount of ethanol. :MC-B: This leaves us with no net gain in the reduction of carbon emissions, or our use of fossil fuel. . . .
	 :MC-C: But there are more problems with corn ethanol.
	 :MC-D: Corn requires more fertilizer to grow strong and healthy than any other major crop. :MC-E: About 40 percent of all nitrogen fertilizer used for growing our crops is used for corn, and the fertilizer is almost all fossil energy.
	 :MC-F: In spite of over 1,000 uses we have for corn and corn byproducts, about 20 percent of corn grown in the United States is now used to produce ethanol, up from 6.5 percent in 2000. . . . (paragraph 14)
